after.description: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS — integrate Contentstack's Live Preview SDK so that content editors see real-time updates in the CMS preview iframe. The integration must plug into the existing content-fetching pipeline (useContent hook) and only activate when the app is running inside the Contentstack Live Preview context, leaving normal production rendering unaffected.
after.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS

notes: Novel story — Contentstack Live Preview is a new capability not present in the codebase. The central attachment point is the useContent hook (imported from hooks/useContent), which is the single funnel all Contentstack components use to fetch content. Live Preview SDK integration would plug into this hook to receive real-time content updates and trigger re-renders. No existing fix site; this is greenfield wiring into an existing data path.

notes: Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria with a valuable note identifying useContent as the single integration funnel. I built the full AC list from the story description and technical context. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 establish the core activation gate — LP only works inside the LP iframe context, production is untouched. (2) AC-3 sets a latency budget of 5 seconds for updates to appear. (3) AC-4 ties the integration to the useContent hook as openspec identified. (4) AC-5/AC-6/AC-7/AC-8/AC-10 cover error and edge cases — SDK load failure, connection drop, rapid updates, unmount race, malformed content. (5) AC-11 addresses script-origin validation as a security concern. (6) AC-12 ensures zero footprint outside LP context. (7) AC-13/AC-14 cover navigation and locale/content-type switching within LP. CAVEAT: Without seeing the actual contents of hooks/useContent, src/services/contentstack.ts, and the mock files, some criteria may need adjustment once the existing API surface and data shapes are known — particularly AC-4 (how useContent exposes data) and AC-10 (what 'malformed' means for the existing content types).
